title: Plan to end chronic homelessness and 2024 funding
subtitle: Fee-for-service housing proposals deferred; A Better Tent City funding request, tax levy impact and a second hybrid shelter debated.
overview: The Community and Health Services Committee recommended that Regional Council begin the interim Plan to End Chronic Homelessness {{vote:m6}}. It adds $11,124,967 to the 2024 Housing Services operating budget, funded from the Tax Stabilization Reserve and the property tax levy. It also amends the capital program for a hybrid shelter and creates a Homelessness Prevention Capital Reserve. Staff said the plan would raise the overall 2024 tax levy increase from 6.7% to 8.3%.

The committee referred a separate set of fee-for-service funding proposals for housing stability providers to the Strategic Planning and Budget Committee meeting on November 22 {{vote:m3}}. Members wanted more information on how proposals were scored. A Better Tent City, which was not recommended for funding, asked for money for dedicated staff.

Both items go to budget deliberations as recommendations, so nothing is final. Residents should expect the 2024 property tax levy, shelter capacity and funding rules for homelessness providers to be debated further. Staff are due to return with a fuller plan by the end of April.

decisions.item: Plan to End Chronic Homelessness: 2024 budget
decisions.detail: The committee recommended adding $11,124,967 to the 2024 Housing Services operating budget, funded by $3,200,000 from the Tax Stabilization Reserve and $7,924,967 from the property tax levy, and starting work with community partners on the plan's initiatives.

decisions.item: Second hybrid shelter and capital reserve
decisions.detail: The committee recommended amending the 2024-2033 Housing capital program for a hybrid shelter and establishing a Homelessness Prevention Capital Reserve.

The committee recommended authorizing Real Estate and Legal Services to negotiate conditional purchase or lease agreements for plan initiatives, with any resulting agreement returning to Regional Council for approval.

The committee recommended that Council advocate to the federal and provincial governments for sustainable homelessness funding, and that staff work with community and area municipalities on policy incentives to create and protect affordable housing.

The committee referred the staff recommendation on 2023 fee-for-service results, including nine proposals totalling $3,113,493, to the Strategic Planning and Budget Committee on November 22, 2023 {{vote:m3}}.

debate: Delegates from A Better Tent City said volunteers can no longer sustain its services and asked for funding for dedicated staff. They said the funding criteria were unclear and that they had been told only that they did not meet them.

Staff said a council-set scoring process was applied by a panel of staff and that proposals were judged on alignment with Housing First principles. They said they would not discuss individual applicants in the meeting but would meet unsuccessful groups. Several councillors asked for more transparency on scoring and a review of the criteria.

Some councillors questioned whether shelter-style options fit Housing First, and whether a second hybrid shelter should proceed before the first is reviewed. They noted few residents had moved to permanent housing so far. Staff said both interim and permanent solutions are needed and that early results were encouraging.

Staff and councillors raised concern about relying on the property tax levy for homelessness services, which staff said is not what the levy was designed for. Members also discussed advocacy to other levels of government and presenting provincial impacts in the budget.

Supporters, including delegates who helped co-create the plan, said it came from broad community collaboration and answers an urgent need. Some councillors said it was ambitious but unclear on deliverables, and others said the timeline to April for a fuller plan was reasonable.
